name: Alaska
rule: We did not read Alaska's deduction rule on its own sites, so only the federal floor below applies here.

name: Arizona
rule: Only if required or empowered by law, with the employee's prior written authorization, or where there is a reasonable good faith dispute over the amount due (including a set-off the employer claims).

name: California
rule: We did not read California's deduction rule on its own sites, so only the federal floor below applies here.

name: Colorado
rule: CDLE allows 10 days to audit that property or money entrusted to the employee was returned; written notice and other requirements apply to deductions in that case. Other deduction rules were not read.

name: Connecticut
rule: Only if required or empowered by law, or with the employee's written authorization on a form approved by the labor commissioner (plus medical deductions without financial benefit to the employer, and automatic retirement enrollment).

name: Delaware
rule: Only if required or empowered by law, for medical care without financial benefit to the employer, or with a signed authorization for a lawful purpose that benefits the employee.

name: District of Columbia
rule: We did not read District of Columbia's deduction rule on its own sites, so only the federal floor below applies here.

name: Hawaii
rule: We did not read Hawaii's deduction rule on its own sites, so only the federal floor below applies here.

name: Idaho
rule: Only if required by law or with written authorization; even then usually not below minimum wage. A proven advance or draw can be withheld in full.

name: Illinois
rule: Not allowed: an employer cannot withhold or deduct pending the return of uniforms, tools or other employer-owned equipment.

name: Iowa
verdict: only if assigned and acknowledged in writing
rule: Lost or stolen property cannot be deducted unless it was equipment specifically assigned to the employee, who acknowledged receipt in writing.

name: Kansas
rule: Allowed from final wages after a written notice and explanation, until the property is returned; then the withheld wages must be paid.

name: Kentucky
rule: We did not read Kentucky's deduction rule on its own sites, so only the federal floor below applies here.

name: Maine
verdict: not a debt the employee owes
rule: Tools of the trade and uniforms primarily for the employer's benefit are not a "debt" an employee can be made to repay from wages, and property damage cannot be set off against a wage claim.

name: Maryland
rule: Only if ordered by a court, authorized expressly in writing by the employee, allowed by the Commissioner because the employee received full consideration, or made under another law.

name: Massachusetts
rule: We did not read Massachusetts's deduction rule on its own sites, so only the federal floor below applies here.

name: Michigan
rule: We did not read Michigan's deduction rule on its own sites, so only the federal floor below applies here.

name: Minnesota
verdict: only with written consent after the loss
rule: Only with the employee's voluntary written authorization given after the loss, or a court judgment.

name: Montana
rule: Reasonable deductions for board, room and other incidentals that are a condition of employment, or as otherwise provided by law. When an employee is discharged over an alleged theft connected to the work, the employer may withhold the value of the theft from the final paycheck if the conditions of 39-3-205(3) are met.

name: New Hampshire
rule: We did not read New Hampshire's deduction rule on its own sites, so only the federal floor below applies here.

name: New Jersey
rule: Not among the deductions N.J.S.A. 34:11-4.4 lists.

name: New York
rule: We did not read New York's deduction rule on its own sites, so only the federal floor below applies here.

name: North Carolina
verdict: allowed with a specific signed authorization
rule: Allowed with a signed written authorization made in advance that names the item and the dollar amount (the department's example: a $150 phone).

name: North Dakota
verdict: allowed with a specific signed authorization
rule: A nonrecurring deduction needs written authorization citing its source; for damage, breakage, shortage or negligence, authorization at the time of the deduction.

name: Oklahoma
rule: We did not read Oklahoma's deduction rule on its own sites, so only the federal floor below applies here.

name: Oregon
rule: Only if legally required, or the employee voluntarily agrees in writing and the deduction is for the employee's benefit.

name: Pennsylvania
rule: We did not read Pennsylvania's deduction rule on its own sites, so only the federal floor below applies here.

name: South Carolina
rule: Only if required or permitted by law, or the employer gave the written notice of the deductions required at hiring (with seven days' written notice of changes).

name: South Dakota
verdict: the check may be held until the property is returned
rule: The final paycheck may be held until the property is returned (a hold, not a deduction).

name: Tennessee
rule: Generally no deductions without the employee's consent in a signed written agreement.

name: Texas
rule: Only if ordered by a court, authorized by law, or with the employee's written authorization for a lawful purpose.

name: Vermont
rule: Allowed deductions are set by Vermont's Minimum Wage Rules (not read here); the department stresses that the employee must still receive at least minimum wage.

name: Virginia
rule: Only taxes, deductions in accordance with law, or with the employee's written and signed authorization.

name: Washington
rule: Only if required by law, specifically agreed orally or in writing by the employee and employer (except as RCW 49.48.160 prohibits), or for medical care recorded in the books.

name: West Virginia
verdict: allowed under a signed itemized agreement and written notice
rule: Allowed up to the replacement cost if the property is worth over $100, the employee signed an itemized agreement with replacement costs when receiving it, and the employer gave written notice and a demand to return it within at most 10 business days; the wages must be released if it is returned.

name: Wyoming
rule: Deductions are allowed in certain cases, including cash shortages, repayment of loans or advances, and damaged or lost equipment, and must follow the wage offset rules (not read here).
